title: Adaptive cohort TTLs and content-hash anchored invalidation for embedding cache
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Reranking and embedding endpoints see variable reuse patterns across tenants and workflows. A static TTL for cached embeddings leads to either wasted memory (TTL too long) or quality regressions/latency spikes (TTL too short triggering recompute). We also see duplicates from near-identical inputs (minor punctuation/whitespace differences) and tenant-specific access patterns that would benefit from cohort-aware caching. Goal: design and deploy an adaptive, cohort-aware TTL system for the embedding cache that uses content-hash anchored invalidation, normalized keying to reduce false duplicates, and a small staleness-detection signal to automatically shorten TTLs for workloads with high embedding drift. The system must be safe to roll out (feature-flagged), observable (per-tenant hit-rate and staleness metric), and cost-neutral or better within one release window.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Cache key normalization implemented: whitespace/punctuation normalization + stable lowercase + model artifact version encoded
2) Content-hash anchored invalidation implemented (content_hash v1) with backward-compatible invalidation hook
3) Cohort detection: automated grouping by tenant + endpoint pattern with per-cohort TTL adjustable by runtime policy
4) TTL adaptation algorithm rollout: initial conservative defaults with automatic reduction when reuse > 4 within TTL and increase when reuse < 1 for 7-day window
5) Implementation behind feature flag and canary to 5% traffic; no customer-facing errors introduced
6) Metrics: achieve >= 20% improvement in global embedding-cache hit-rate on canary tenants or equivalent latency reduction (p95 embedding latency reduced by >= 15ms)
7) Documentation: runbook for invalidation and manual TTL override in Console
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge behind feature flag; unit + integration tests. Dry-run metrics collection enabled (no eviction) - 2 days
Phase 1: Canary to 5% of traffic (select tenants with low risk) - monitor hit-rate, p95/p99 latency, cost delta - 3 days
Phase 2: Expand to 25% if metrics stable; enable adaptive TTL for cohorts only (deny-list high-risk customers) - 4 days
Phase 3: Full rollout to all hosted tenants with manual override in Console; enable content-hash invalidation hook for Private customers via opt-in - ongoing
metrics: Embedding cache hit rate (per-cohort and global)
Embedding endpoint p95 and p99 latency (ms)
Number of embedding recomputes per 1000 requests
Memory use of cache (GB) and cost per 1M requests
Staleness signal: fraction of hits whose cosine similarity to recomputed embedding < 0.92
notes: Design decision: use content_hash v1 = blake3(hex(normalized_input + model_version + tenant_salt)) to keep key length small and deterministic across languages.
Trade-offs: stronger normalization reduces duplicate cache entries but risks merging semantically distinct inputs; we add a conservative normalization step and an allowlist for exact-mode callers.
Sharding: cache key includes consistent-shard prefix to preserve hot-key distribution. We will use tenant-aware consistent hashing to reduce thundering-herd during invalidation.
Eviction policy: LRU per-shard with cohort-priority boost for high-reuse cohorts. We will add a small admission policy to avoid cold churn.

Staleness detection: lightweight background sampler recomputes embeddings for a small % of hits and reports drift; cohorts exceeding drift threshold will have TTL shortened automatically and trigger a rebuild queue for warmup.
Privacy: content_hash uses tenant_salt; for Private deployments we expose an opt-in endpoint to rotate tenant_salt for full control.

Benchmarks (prototype, internal): on a 48-hour sample of search and chat workloads, normalized keys + dedupe + cohort TTLs produced +22% hit-rate and median embedding latency drop of 12ms; p95 improved by 35ms for canary tenants. Memory increased by ~6% but recompute cost dropped ~18%.
